data.content_ref: inline:The analogy's 'overturn_conditions' are framed as refuting an analogy, but both conditions actually corroborate the claim under review. If the driver (panel) 'consistently overrides the navigator (checklist) on divergence cases and is more often correct,' this supports the expert-intuition side of the debate, not the checklist side; and if the checklist is 'not the source of reliability' but the panel is still correct due to 'independent local knowledge,' the panel's gain is not checklist-driven. Yet the target never establishes what the analogy argues FOR or AGAINST in the first place, so it fails to take a stance on the claim it is supposed to evaluate.
